  const ast = parseTextToAST(text);

  visit(ast, type as string, (node) => {
    positions.push(node.position);

        let world = worldOf(input);
        let domain = domainOf(input);
        if (domain != atomSource(atom))
            Err(atomName(atom) + " needs " + domainName(atomSource(atom))
                + " but the current domain is " + domainName(domain) + ".")
        else match List.find(fact -> fact#world != world, facts) {
            case Some(_) => Err("a fact from another world cannot apply here.")
            case None =>
                let targets = List.filterMap(fact ->
                    if (fact#atom == atom and holds(input, fact#source)) Some(fact#target) else None,
                    facts);
                Ok(frontierOf(world, atomTarget(atom), targets))
        }
    }

pub def lexicalTokens(text: String): List[String] =
        List.distinct(List.filter(token -> String.length(token) >= 3, tokenize(String.toList(String.toLowerCase(text)), "", Nil)))

    def tokenize(chars: List[Char], current: String, acc: List[String]): List[String] = match chars {
        case Nil => flushToken(current, acc)
        case c :: rest =>
            if (isTokenChar(c)) tokenize(rest, current + "${c}", acc)
            else tokenize(rest, "", flushToken(current, acc))
    }

    def flushToken(current: String, acc: List[String]): List[String] =
        if (String.isEmpty(current)) acc else current :: acc

pub def similarityOrder(left: Scored, right: Scored): Comparison = {
        let leftPath = fst(left);
        let leftScore = snd(left);
        let rightPath = fst(right);
        let rightScore = snd(right);
        if (leftScore > rightScore) Comparison.LessThan
        else if (leftScore < rightScore) Comparison.GreaterThan
        else if (leftPath < rightPath) Comparison.LessThan
        else if (leftPath > rightPath) Comparison.GreaterThan
        else Comparison.EqualTo
    }

            and List.length(candidate#outputs) >= 1
            and List.length(candidate#outputs) <= maxOutputs()
            and List.length(List.distinct(candidate#outputs)) == List.length(candidate#outputs)
            and List.forAll(output -> bound(output, atoms), candidate#outputs)
            and List.length(candidate#denied) <= maxInequalities()
            and List.forAll(pair -> match pair {
                case (left, right) => left != right and bound(left, atoms) and bound(right, atoms)
            }, candidate#denied)
    }

    def slotInRange(slot: Int32): Bool = slot >= 0 and slot < maxRoles()

domains.html:
/// One role slot must mean one nominal domain. The domains come from the core
    /// signature table, so an atom that reads a role as a file and an atom that
    /// writes it as a symbol cannot be composed into one conjunction.
    def domainsConsistent(atoms: List[AtomPattern]): Bool =
        List.forAll(role -> List.length(List.distinct(domainsOf(role, atoms))) <= 1, List.distinct(roleList(atoms)))

    def domainsOf(role: Int32, atoms: List[AtomPattern]): List[Domain] =
        List.flatMap(atom ->
            (if (atom#subject == role) Attune.atomSource(atom#relation) :: Nil else Nil)
                ::: (if (atom#object == role) Attune.atomTarget(atom#relation) :: Nil else Nil),
            atoms)

canonical.html:
/// The canonical descriptor: the least of the consistent renamings, with the
    /// atoms sorted and de-duplicated and the roles renumbered by first
    /// appearance.
    pub def canonical(candidate: Descriptor): Descriptor =
        match bestOption(candidate, renamings(), None) {
            case None         => emptyDescriptor()
            case Some(option) => renumber(renamed(candidate, option))
        }

    /// The canonical identity key. Two descriptors share it exactly when they are
    /// the same candidate up to a consistent renaming of their role slots.
    pub def identityKey(candidate: Descriptor): String = render(canonical(candidate))

population.html:
/// The deterministic bounded population: unsafe descriptors and duplicates
    /// removed, one descriptor per candidate id, sorted by canonical identity.
    pub def population(candidates: List[Candidate]): Population = {
        let ordered = List.sortBy(candidate -> candidate#id, candidates);
        let (conflicts, unique) = resolveIds(ordered, Nil, Nil, Nil);
        let canonicalCandidates = List.map(candidate ->
            { id = candidate#id, descriptor = canonical(candidate#descriptor) }, unique);
        let admitted = List.filter(candidate -> safe(candidate#descriptor), canonicalCandidates);
        let distinct = dedupIdentities(admitted, Nil, Nil);
        let kept = List.sortBy(candidate -> identityKey(candidate#descriptor), distinct);
        let bounded = List.take(maxCandidates(), kept);
        {
            kept = bounded,
            dropped = List.length(candidates) - List.length(bounded),
            conflicts = List.reverse(conflicts),
            truncated = List.length(kept) > maxCandidates()
        }
    }

shards.html:
/// Split one population into world-level shards at the declared granularity.
    pub def shards(population: Population): Shards = {
        let all = if (List.isEmpty(population#kept)) Nil else chunks(shardSize(), population#kept);
        let bounded = List.take(maxShards(), all);
        let total = List.foldLeft((count, shard) -> count + List.length(shard), 0, bounded);
        { shards = bounded, dropped = List.length(population#kept) - total, truncated = List.length(all) > maxShards() }
    }

reuse.html:
// shape projection: the two declared output slots of one binding.
        Output(c, w, role(out0, e0, e1, e2, e3), role(out1, e0, e1, e2, e3)) :-
            Binding(c, w, e0, e1, e2, e3),

        // anchored application join: a task or pair context joins an anchor to an
        // already materialized structural row and never re-evaluates the structure.
        Task(c, w, x, y) :- Output(c, w, x, y), Anchor(w, x).

promotion.html:
/// Whether an outcome promotes its candidate. Only `Relevant` does.
    pub def promotes(outcome: JevOutcome): Bool = outcome == JevOutcome.Relevant

    /// The frozen stable promotion key `(Relevant ? 0 : 1, original base rank)`.
    pub def promotionKey(outcome: JevOutcome, baseRank: Int32): (Int32, Int32) =
        (if (promotes(outcome)) 0 else 1, baseRank)

qwen.html:
/// The frozen similarity of one query and one candidate vector: cosine on the
    /// two unnormalized hosted vectors, computed by the shared declared statement
    /// of the embedding branch.
    pub def cosine(searchVector: List[Float64], candidate: List[Float64]): Float64 =
        Embedding.cosine(searchVector, candidate)

    /// The complete standalone Q ranking of one candidate population against one
    /// query, under the same frozen similarity/order statement as every other
    /// embedding arm. No candidate is dropped and no rank is invented.
    pub def rankBySimilarity(searchVector: List[Float64], candidates: List[(String, List[Float64])]): List[Embedding.Entry] =
        Embedding.rankBySimilarity(searchVector, candidates)

inverse.html:
/// The opposite of one directed atom. `defines`/`defined_in`,
    /// `imports`/`imported_by` and `calls`/`callers` are the three inverse
    /// pairs. Deriving an inverse relation reads this one typed table rather
    /// than a second string mapping, so the forward and inverse vocabularies
    /// cannot disagree.
    pub def inverse(atom: Atom): Atom = match atom {
        case Atom.Defines    => Atom.DefinedIn
        case Atom.DefinedIn  => Atom.Defines
        case Atom.Imports    => Atom.ImportedBy
        case Atom.ImportedBy => Atom.Imports
        case Atom.Calls      => Atom.Callers
        case Atom.Callers    => Atom.Calls
    }

bindingNotes.html:
// shape 0>1;2>1
// Record one match. c = question ID; w = source world.
// e0, e1, e2 are the values filling positions 0, 1, 2.
// The last e0 fills an unused fourth slot in the fixed row format.
Binding(c, w, e0, e1, e2, e0) :-
// Read the recipe for question c: shape, relations, inequality, outputs.
// _ means this line does not need that column’s value.
Desc(c, shape, r0, r1, r2, _, neq0, neq1, _, _),
// Find a first edge in world w, using relationship r0: e0 -> e1.
Edge(w, r0, e0, e1),
// Find a second edge in the SAME world, using r1: e2 -> e1.
// Repeating e1 makes the two edges share their target.
Edge(w, r1, e2, e1),
// Use this rule only for the shared-target wiring.
if (shape == "0>1;2>1"),
// Enforce each optional "these two positions must differ" check.
// A test passes when this is not the requested pair, OR the values differ.
// In the frozen 72-question family no pair is required to differ.
if (neq0 != 0 or neq1 != 1 or e0 != e1),
if (neq0 != 0 or neq1 != 2 or e0 != e2),
if (neq0 != 1 or neq1 != 2 or e1 != e2).

theoryHTML:
Start with a file we already found.

In Greenwood #1100, Qwen put bundle.js first. That gives us a useful starting point, but it is only one part of the fix.

The question is simple: what helper does this file use, and who else uses that helper?

Read the arrows as sentences.

bundle.js imports resource-utils.js. That is the first recorded fact.

graph.js also imports resource-utils.js. That is the second. To find graph.js from the helper, read this import backward: “this helper is imported by graph.js.”

Together, those facts tell us that two build stages use the same helper. They do not tell us that both stages have a bug.

bundle.js ------> resource-utils.js <------ graph.js
           uses                    used by

Atlas calls these steps: Imports ; ImportedBy

What Theory.flix contributes

Theory checks that both arrows really exist in the same source snapshot and meet at the same helper. It will not fill a missing arrow with a guess.

Think of its work as a sentence with blanks:

Start at this file. Find a file it imports. Return another file that imports that same file.

This is an English explanation of a relation composition, not executable Flix. The browser displays the census’s saved match; it does not run Theory again.

Finding a connection is not the same as finding the fix.

The shared helper was only 28th in Qwen’s list. It stayed 28th with Jev alone. With graph information supplied to Jev, it moved to 10th.

That change matters: Greenwood went from an incomplete result to all eight fixing files in the top ten.

The recorded connection makes the helper’s role understandable. The study does not establish that this particular pair of arrows caused Jev’s decision.

One small piece of the actual Flix

This rule keeps a matched pair only when its first member is the chosen starting point. Read :- as “when” and the comma as “and.”

In English: keep this result when the connection matched, and it starts where we asked. w is the source snapshot, x the starting point, and y the result. c identifies the connection description.

The larger implementation also checks file and symbol types and gives equivalent descriptions a consistent identity. Those checks protect the match; they do not read an issue or assign a relevance score.
